title: Income v capital — profit-making schemes (Myer, s 25A ITAA 1936, s 15-15 ITAA 1997)
summary: Facet map: is a profit on sale income or capital? Spine: date/regime (s 25A(1A) pre-20/9/1985 only; s 25A(1B) pre-1997-98 only — else s 15-15/Myer/CGT) → profit-making purpose at acquisition → Myer three conditions (purpose, commercial dealing, not mere realisation — Myer Emporium (1987) 163 CLR 199) → mere realisation boundary (Scottish Australian Mining (1950), Whitfords Beach (1982)) → income (s 6-5 or s 15-15) or capital (CGT) → legacy s 25A deeming cascade (ss 25A(2)-(10)) with the s 25A(3) Commissioner discretion. FACETS: Myer conditions detail, mere realisation doctrine, s 15-15 statutory limb, the s 25A(2)-(10) deeming cascade, s 25A(3) discretion, timing/derivation. Subsection coverage: s 25A(1), (1A), (1B), (2)-(12) all mapped; s 15-15(1)-(2) mapped. s 25A(11): prescribed-manner transfers (gift, below-market, non-arm's-length; or distributions of non-excepted property). s 25A(12): definitions of excepted property (trading stock, plant), private company, private trust estate, and property includes interests. Rulings: TR 92/3, TR 1995/33.

nodes.label: You sell property and realise a profit — income or capital?
nodes.body: The single question with the most facets in Australian tax. Spine: date/regime → profit-making purpose → Myer scheme → mere realisation boundary → statutory/legacy limbs. Facets carry the case-law signposts and deeming machinery.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits
Profit-making undertaking or plan

nodes.label: When was the property acquired, and in which year did the profit arise?
nodes.body: s 25A(1A) — ACQUISITION DATE TEST: s 25A does NOT apply to sale of property acquired on or after 20 September 1985 (post-CGT property). For post-CGT property: analyse under s 6-5 ordinary income (Myer) and CGT Part 3-1. s 15-15(2)(b) also excludes profits from sale of post-CGT property. s 25A(1B) — PROFIT YEAR / UNDERTAKING TEST: s 25A does NOT apply to a profit arising 1997-98+ from a profit-making undertaking or scheme (even if the undertaking was entered into pre-1997-98). Such profits are dealt with under s 15-15 ITAA 1997. Pre-CGT property with pre-1997-98 profit (or not from an undertaking/scheme): s 25A legacy applies.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits
Profit-making undertaking or plan

nodes.label: Apply the modern framework: Myer (s 6-5) + CGT (s 15-15 limited by s 15-15(2))
nodes.body: For post-20/9/1985 property: s 6-5 ordinary income (Myer principle) and CGT Part 3-1 for capital gains. s 15-15 ITAA 1997 does NOT apply to profits arising from the sale of property acquired on or after 20 September 1985 (s 15-15(2)(b)). s 15-15 may apply to non-property-sale profit-making undertakings or plans where s 15-15(2)(a)-(b) does not exclude it.

statute.title: Profit-making undertaking or plan

nodes.label: Apply s 25A directly (pre-1985 property or pre-1997-98 profit)
nodes.body: s 25A(1): profit from (a) sale of property acquired for profit-making by sale, or (b) a profit-making undertaking or scheme. Deeming rules in ss 25A(2)-(10) extend this.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: Was the property acquired for the purpose of profit-making by sale?
nodes.body: The gateway for s 25A(1)(a): was the property acquired for the purpose of profit-making by sale? Purpose must exist at acquisition and be the dominant/prevailing purpose, evidenced objectively. TR 1995/33 discusses subjective purpose. NOTE: s 15-15 ITAA 1997 has NO acquisition-purpose requirement — it applies to profit from a profit-making undertaking or plan regardless of acquisition purpose. s 15-15(2) excludes profits already ordinary income or from post-CGT property sales.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

rulings.title: relevance of subjective purpose, motive or intention

nodes.label: Did you carry on a profit-making undertaking or scheme (Myer Emporium)?
nodes.body: Myer Emporium Ltd v FCT (1987) 163 CLR 199: profit on an isolated transaction is ordinary income where (1) purpose of profit-making at entry, (2) the transaction is a commercial dealing, (3) the profit is not a mere realisation of a capital asset. Operates through s 6-5.

statute.title: Income according to ordinary concepts (ordinary income)

cases.note: Myer Emporium Ltd v FCT (1987) 163 CLR 199

nodes.label: Was there an undertaking or scheme (a commercial operation), not a mere realisation?
nodes.body: Mere realisation of a capital asset is NOT income (Scottish Australian Mining (1950); FCT v Whitfords Beach (1982)). An organised commercial operation with profit purpose IS income. The line: extent of activity — subdivision, development, marketing, organised selling.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits
Profit-making undertaking or plan

nodes.label: Mere realisation — capital, not income
nodes.body: Capital gain under CGT (Part 3-1) for post-CGT assets; not assessable for pre-CGT assets. Scottish Australian Mining (1950), Whitfords Beach (1982).

nodes.label: Assessable as ordinary income (Myer) or statutory income (s 15-15)
nodes.body: Profit from a profit-making scheme is assessable: s 6-5 ordinary income (Myer) or s 15-15 statutory income. s 15-15 applies only where s 15-15(2) exclusions are not met: the profit is not already ordinary income under s 6-5, and does not arise from sale of post-CGT property. Otherwise the amount is s 6-5 ordinary income or capital/CGT.

statute.title: Profit-making undertaking or plan

nodes.label: Do the s 25A(2)-(10) deeming rules apply (shares/interests in entities holding profit-making property)?
nodes.body: s 25A(2): Subject to s 25A(3) discretion, where AFTER 23 AUGUST 1983 a taxpayer sells shares in a private company, a partnership interest, or an interest in a private trust estate, AND at the time of sale the entity held property that: (i) was acquired for profit-making by sale AND (ii) was NOT excepted property (i.e., not trading stock or plant used for producing assessable income — see s 25A(12)(a)); OR through interposed entities held property acquired for profit-making by sale and not excepted property — the taxpayer is deemed to have acquired the relevant property for profit-making by sale. s 25A(3): Commissioner discretion NOT to apply, considering assets, control, other sales, and other matters. ss 25A(4)-(8): bonus shares, rights, prescribed transfers, merged interests, underlying property. ss 25A(9)-(10): Commissioner determines the profit amount. s 25A(11): defines 'prescribed manner' transfers. s 25A(12): defines 'excepted property', 'private company', 'private trust estate', and 'property' includes interests.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: Deemed profit-making purpose — profit assessable under s 25A
nodes.body: Property deemed acquired for profit-making by sale; profit (Commissioner-determined under s 25A(9)) included under s 25A(1).

nodes.label: No deeming — capital (CGT) or not assessable
nodes.body: Post-CGT asset: capital gain subject to CGT (50% discount for individuals/trusts where applicable). Pre-CGT asset: not assessable.

nodes.label: Analysis complete
nodes.body: Profit is: (1) ordinary income (Myer, s 6-5); (2) statutory income (s 15-15); (3) assessable under s 25A (legacy); or (4) capital (CGT) / not assessable. Signposts: purpose at acquisition, commercial operation vs mere realisation, deeming provisions. TR 92/3 is the ATO's key guidance.

nodes.label: FACET — The Myer three conditions and their application
nodes.body: Where to look: Myer Emporium Ltd v FCT (1987) 163 CLR 199; TR 92/3; CCH 'isolated-transactions-myer-principle'. The three conditions: (1) purpose of profit-making at the time of entering the transaction (not merely at sale); (2) the transaction is a business operation or commercial transaction; (3) the profit is not a mere realisation of a capital asset. The principle applies to losses as well as profits (a Myer loss is deductible under s 8-1 if the transaction was a commercial dealing entered into for profit).

statute.title: Income according to ordinary concepts (ordinary income)

cases.note: Myer Emporium Ltd v FCT (1987) 163 CLR 199

nodes.label: FACET — The mere realisation doctrine and its limits
nodes.body: Where to look: Scottish Australian Mining Co Ltd v FCT (1950) 81 CLR 188 (subdividing and selling a mining property remained realisation); FCT v Whitfords Beach Pty Ltd (1982) 150 CLR 355 (company formed to develop land — business, not mere realisation); Californian Copper Syndicate v Harris (1904) (classic statement). The doctrine: profits from mere realisation, even with effort to enhance saleability, are capital unless the taxpayer is carrying on a business of selling or entered a profit-making scheme.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

cases.note: Scottish Australian Mining Co Ltd v FCT (1950) 81 CLR 188
FCT v Whitfords Beach Pty Ltd (1982) 150 CLR 355

nodes.label: FACET — s 15-15 ITAA 1997 (the statutory limb)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 15-15 ITAA 1997. s 15-15(1): Your assessable income includes profit arising from the carrying on or carrying out of a profit-making undertaking or plan. s 15-15(2): This section does NOT apply to a profit that: (a) is assessable as ordinary income under s 6-5; or (b) arises in respect of the sale of property acquired on or after 20 September 1985. s 25A(1B) diverts post-1997-98 profit-making undertaking/scheme profits to s 15-15 (subject to the s 15-15(2) exclusions). s 15-15 has no subsection (3).

statute.title: Profit-making undertaking or plan

nodes.label: FACET — The s 25A(2)-(10) deeming cascade in detail
nodes.body: Where to look: s 25A(2) (private company shares / partnership interests / private trust interests deemed profit-making where the entity holds profit-making property — sub-para (b)(i) direct, (b)(ii) through interposed entities); s 25A(3) (Commissioner's discretion having regard to assets, control, other sales); s 25A(4) (bonus shares and rights); s 25A(5) (prescribed transfers); s 25A(6)-(8) (merged interests, underlying property, transferred property); s 25A(9)-(10) (Commissioner determines the profit amount, with the pre-1985 adjustment).

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: FACET — The s 25A(3) Commissioner discretion
nodes.body: Where to look: s 25A(3) — the Commissioner may decide s 25A(2) should NOT apply, considering: (a) the extent to which the entity's assets consisted of the profit-making property immediately before sale; (b) the nature and extent of the taxpayer's control of the entity; (c) circumstances of other sales of interests in the entity; (d) such other matters as the Commissioner considers relevant. A protective discretion — the taxpayer can request it not be applied.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: FACET — Timing and year of derivation
nodes.body: Where to look: s 6-5 derivation principles for ordinary income (receipts basis or earnings basis depending on the taxpayer's business structure); CGT event A1 timing at disposal (contract date, s 104-10(3) ITAA 1997). For s 15-15 profits, the year of derivation follows ordinary statutory income principles (derived when the profit is realised or receivable). s 25A(9) deems the profit amount (Commissioner-determined) but does not determine the year of derivation. The income/capital character must be determined as at acquisition.

statute.title: Profit-making undertaking or plan

nodes.label: No profit-making purpose — capital or not assessable
nodes.body: If no profit-making purpose at acquisition, s 25A(1)(a) does not apply. Post-CGT asset: capital gain subject to CGT (Part 3-1). Pre-CGT asset: not assessable (unless a profit-making undertaking or scheme under s 25A(1)(b) or Myer/s 6-5 or s 15-15 applies).

nodes.label: Apply s 15-15 ITAA 1997 (profit-making undertaking or plan)
nodes.body: s 25A(1B) diverts post-1997-98 profits from profit-making undertakings/schemes to s 15-15 ITAA 1997. s 15-15(1): Your assessable income includes profit arising from the carrying on or carrying out of a profit-making undertaking or plan. s 15-15(2): This section does NOT apply if the profit: (a) is assessable as ordinary income under s 6-5; or (b) arises from sale of post-CGT property. Since this is pre-CGT property, s 15-15(2)(b) does not apply. Check whether the profit is already ordinary income under s 6-5 (Myer conditions) — if so, s 15-15(2)(a) excludes it and s 6-5 applies instead.

statute.title: Profit-making undertaking or plan

nodes.label: FACET — s 25A(11) prescribed-manner transfers and s 25A(12) definitions
nodes.body: Where to look: s 25A(11)-(12) ITAA 1936. s 25A(11): Property is transferred in the 'prescribed manner' if: (a) by way of gift or below-market consideration, NOT by will/intestacy, and the parties were not at arm's length; OR (b) by way of distribution of non-excepted property from a private company or private trust estate to a shareholder/beneficiary. s 25A(12): 'Excepted property' means: (a)(i) trading stock; (a)(ii) plant purchased for producing assessable income. 'Private company' = company whose shares are not listed. 'Private trust estate' = trust whose units are not listed or publicly available. 'Property' includes an estate or interest in property.
